preview: Interview experience of Virik Jain for the Technology Analyst (FTE) role at Morgan Stanley, detailing the online test and three interview rounds.
content:
VIRIK JAIN, BTech CS 2017-21 
 
• Company: Morgan Stanley 
• Job description or Role: Technology Analyst (FTE) 
 
 
 
• 
Test information 
Online Round on AMCAT having 3 sections:  
1) Debugging (7 Qs, 20 mins): very basic Qs like find error in logic, missing semicolon, etc  
 
2) Aptitude (10 Qs, 20 mins): Basic maths, logic based aptitude and data interpretation Qs; except a few, most of them were easy 
 
3) Coding (3 Qs, 1hr): Qs were basic but problem statement is slightly convoluted; 1 Math, 1 Graph(BFS/DFS) and 1 hashing+sorting 
 
• 
Interview Process 
2 Technical + 1 HR/Pro-fit 
Round 1 (20 students): 
– Asked me to describe one of my projects, but didn’t ask any Qs on it 
– Discussion on Time Complexity: how is it measured, compare some complexities 
– Function call and return mechanism in OS (ie. function call stack) 
– Suggest a data structure to use based on given requirement (eg: what will you use to implement whatsapp search autocomplete feature? Ans: Trie) 
– Hashing and why and when to use it 
– DSA Qs (find frequency of all characters in a string, find 2nd largest element in an array, find kth largest element in an array, mirror a binary tree) 
– 32 bit vs 64 bit processor 
– Describe Virtual vs Physical memory 
– Asked if I have any question for him (ask anything, for example, the tech stack or projects in the company, but do ask something) 
Round 2 (12 students): 
– Asked me to describe one of my projects, but again no Qs on it 
– Given a boolean matrix (0/1 matrix) where the rows are sorted, find the row with the most number of 1s (gave N*M, NlogM and N+M solutions) 
– Design a data structure that supports all the given 3 queries in O(1) 
1) Insert(x): insert ‘x’ in the data structure 
2) Search(x): return true if ‘x’ exists in data structure, else false 
3) Add(x): add ‘x’ to ALL the elements that are currently in the data structure 
The queries can be in any order. (Hint: Maintain a cumulative sum of all ‘x’ for all Add(x) queries) 
– Design a food delivery system like Swiggy 
I mentioned the different functionalities and the entities in the system. I was then asked to describe the attributes of the entities. This was more discussion based rather than a Q&A; you should be vocal and describe all your design choices and in a few cases justify why you chose one choice over the other. The interviewer will question your choices, that’s fine, it doesn’t mean you are wrong. You need to justify your choice in such case or accept a change in your choice and justify the change. 
– Asked if I had any question for him 
Round 3(~4 students): 
– Asked about what is an important life ethic/characteristic for me 
– Then asked situational Qs (what would you do in case of a disagreement with your team members, what would you do if your childhood friend is breaking company rules, etc) 
– Asked if I had any question for him 
– (some people were asked a few technical design Qs too in this round, but due to time constraints, I wasn’t asked any technical Qs in this round) 
 
Finally, 2 of us were selected for Technology Analyst role.
